transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because lately my brain just feels like it completely stalls out. I'll be at work—I'm an engineering tech—and I'll sit there with a test report open, or even just a really simple CAD note. And an hour will go by, and I just can't decide what the next sentence should be, or... or which checkbox I need to click. It's like I just can't think straight enough to make a simple decision.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I just... I don't really care about much lately. I used to be really into 3D printing miniatures, but my printer has just been sitting there with the same half-finished figure on it for months. I haven't even touched it. And things like yoga, or going for a walk in the woods... I used to really like doing those things, but now it just feels like another chore. It's just another task I have to do, instead of something I actually want to do. So I just don't do them.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of things, even when there isn't a clear reason to be concerned?

No, not really. Um, I wouldn't say I worry about things like that. It's not like my mind is racing or anything... it's actually kind of the opposite. Everything just feels really blank and slow, so I don't really have the energy to worry about random stuff.
